title: First 500ms — Developer Voice & Pricing Notes
summary: Working notes: a compact set of developer-facing value props, ultra-fast quickstart angles (first-500ms framing), and pricing language candidates to A/B test in onboarding flows and pricing pages.
body:
Context / why this doc exists:
- We keep tuning messaging to reduce time-to-value friction for engineers evaluating Hosted API. The hypothesis: 'first-500ms' framing (speed to a meaningful result) + transparent unit economics reduces hesitation and increases trial-to-paid conversion.

Objectives:
- Create short, testable microcopy for: signup, 'first request' walkthrough, and pricing panels.
- Produce 3 distinct value-prop arcs aimed at: solo devs/prototypers, engineering leads evaluating latency/cost, and platform/product teams needing scale/SLAs.
- Provide pricing language that feels granular and predictable (no scary comma numbers).

Core developer-first value props (working bullets — informal):
1) Ship measurable features in minutes, not weeks: SDK + ready endpoints + per-route examples mean your first inference should be in under 10 minutes. Microcopy candidate: "From repo to first response in ~10m (no infra)."
2) Pay for what matters: token-based metering + transparent per-request examples. Show concrete sample call costs next to code snippets. Microcopy: "Estimate cost per call before you run it."
3) Predictable performance at scale: per-model latency profiles and route-level SLOs. Microcopy: "Choose performance, not surprises."
4) Safety & private-by-default paths: hosted with optional dedicated/private migrations. Microcopy: "Start hosted. Move private when you need to."

First-500ms framing — what it is:
- Recenter the onboarding story from 'how to use' to 'how fast you see value'. 'First 500ms' refers to the idea that the perceived responsiveness of an LLM integration (from user click to visible reply) should be sub-second for interactive apps. Our ask to devs: get a representative path working and measure latency within your first session.

Quickstart angles (three tested flows):
A) Minimal Demo (solo dev):
- Headline: "See a reply in under a minute"
- Steps: create API key (1m), paste SDK snippet (30s), run sample prompt (10s), inspect output/cost estimate (10s).
- KPI to track: time from sign-up to first successful response; drop-off events at code paste and sample run.
- Microcopy for CTA: "Run a quick reply"

B) Integrate & Measure (engineering lead):
- Headline: "Add an endpoint, measure latency, estimate cost"
- Steps: create route with concurrency guard (2–3m), run 100 synthetic calls via provided script, show latency histogram + per-token cost breakdown.
- KPI: % of teams that create a route and run the synthetic test within 48h.
- CTA microcopy: "Run performance test"

C) Early platform path (platform/product teams):
- Headline: "From prototype to SLA-backed serving"
- Steps: prototype on hosted API (10–60m), request Dedicated trial, map current qps -> reserved capacity estimate via calculator.
- KPI: conversion rate from hosted usage to Dedicated trial request.

Pricing-language drafts (tone: concrete, low-friction, example-driven):
- Principle: always show an example. Pricing lines alone are abstract; concrete examples (3 examples per tier) convert better.

Option 1 (Simple anchors):
- "$0.0009 / token (base model) — e.g., 1 short reply (50 tokens) ≈ $0.045, 1 long reply (1,000 tokens) ≈ $0.90"
- Pros: direct math; cons: token conversation still abstract for many.

Option 2 (Use-case bundles):
- "Starter dev bundle: 10,000 tokens free for 30d — good for prototyping a chat widget or summary pipeline."
- Provide 3 quick mappings: chat message (50 tokens), document summary (800 tokens), embedding call (1 unit per 1,024 tokens).

Option 3 (Predictable Slices):
- "Latency-first plan: higher per-token price, guaranteed p99 latency < 400ms. Cost example: 100k tokens/month -> $X/month."
- "Economy plan: best per-token price, best for batch jobs and background embeddings."

Language to avoid: jargon like 'per-inference compute units' or abstract 'model units' without mapping. Avoid trailing disclaimers on pricing pages; prefer inline clarifying examples.

Competitive positioning notes (short, pragmatic):
- OpenAI: strength = ubiquity + fine-tuned tasks. Our angle: predictable latency profiles + routing to cheaper model variants automatically (sell control/composability).
- Anthropic: safety-first branding. Our angle: production controls + route-level observability + easy Dedicated/pvt migrations.
- Cloud vendors (AWS Sagemaker, Vertex): strength = existing infra contracts. Our angle: developer ergonomics + out-of-box lower total cost for small/medium workloads + faster ramp from prototype to SLA by productized offering.

Objections & rebuttals (developer-centric):
- "I can run an open model myself for cheaper" -> Rebuttal: infra time + ops cost + regression risk. Provide a simple TCO example: 1 engineer @ $X/month to maintain infra vs hosted predictable per-token price and SLAs.
- "Pricing is confusing" -> Rebuttal: show three concrete example calls next to price; include an in-console cost estimator.

Microcopy candidates to A/B test (short snippets):
- CTA variants: "Run a quick reply", "Try a sample request", "Get a reply in 30s"
- Pricing panel lead: "Typical call: 50 tokens ≈ $0.045" vs "Typical call: 1 chat message ≈ $0.05"
- Error handling UX: "Fallback to smaller model (saves cost)" vs "Automatically fall back to a compatible model"

Measurement plan (what to instrument):
- Funnel: signup -> key creation -> paste code -> run sample -> check cost estimate -> integrate. Measure time-to-first-call and p99 latency observed in console during initial 24h.
- Experiment matrix: CTA copy (3x) x pricing example style (3x) x quickstart flow (2x). Primary metric: trial-to-billed conversion within 14d. Secondary: avg time-to-first-call.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need exact per-token prices for each model family (ask pricing ops).
- Get a simple TCO worksheet from infra to show comparison numbers for self-host vs hosted.
- Draft UI mockups for onboarding with cost estimator (ask product-design).

Notes to self (rough):
- Keep code snippets minimal and with inline cost comment so a dev can copy/paste and see a predicted dollar value.
- Consider one-line metric in signup email: "You’ll see your first reply in under a minute — try the quick run in the console."

Links / references used while drafting:
- RDWD-4321: onboarding funnel instrumentation
- Quickstart template PR: github.com/redwood-inference/quickstart-templates/pull/78

End of doc — this is a living draft. Prioritize tests that measure time-to-first-value and perceived pricing clarity in the first 14 days of trial usage.
